title: Busier than ever, earning less
units_note: All money figures in ₹ lakh unless marked. Costs are shown in brackets, e.g. (14.0).

brief.headline: Orders up 12%. Revenue down 5%. Nobody can explain it.
brief.story: SparkWash runs 9 laundry stores across Hyderabad, plus app-based pickup and drop. September was its busiest month ever: 11,000 orders and more clothes washed than ever. Yet revenue fell and profit nearly vanished. Prices haven't changed since April. The founder wants an answer before paying salaries on the 1st.

body.text: Revenue is after discounts. Discounts were ₹0.8L in both months. Refunds for late pickups were ₹0.2L in both months.

bonus.question: What should SparkWash do first?
options: Fix the app checkout so express items are charged ₹180/kg again
bonus.explanation: The price list is right; the app is charging the wrong price. Fixing the checkout restores about ₹6L a month. Raising prices or cutting express punishes customers for a software bug.

explanation.answer: Since the 2 Sep app update merged standard and express into one cart, express orders are being charged ₹90/kg instead of ₹180/kg. Express kilos rose 23% but express revenue fell 36%: ₹6.9L for 7,400 kg is about ₹93 a kilo. At the correct price September revenue would have been about ₹48L, up 9%.
fastest_path: Open revenue by service. Express fell from ₹10.8L to ₹6.9L while everything else grew.
Open orders & kilos. Express kilos rose to 7,400. ₹6.9L ÷ 7,400 kg is about ₹93/kg, roughly the standard rate, not ₹180.
traps: Rising water and detergent costs are real, but costs can't lower revenue.
"Customers switched to standard" is the natural guess, but express kilos went up.
The happy review ("same-day for the normal price!") is the clue hiding in plain sight.
explanation.lesson: When volume goes up and revenue goes down, check the price actually charged, not the price list.
